title: Architecture Standards: Integrated Guidelines and ADRs
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards: API, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes the most impactful Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) affecting serving and infra. The goal is a single reference that teams can cite when designing or reviewing services and model-serving integrations.

Scope

- Applies to all services and repos owned by engineering (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployment artifacts).
- Includes public-facing REST and SDK interfaces, internal microservices, and model-serving runtime components.
- Does not replace team-level runbooks or service-specific design docs; it defines baseline expectations.

Principles

1. Predictability: APIs and runtime behavior must be stable and versioned to avoid breaking producer/consumer contracts.
2. Observability by default: Every service must emit metrics, traces, and structured logs with documented schemas.
3. Production-first: Design and test for operational characteristics (latency, availability, cost) before feature parity.
4. Least privilege: Network, IAM, and secret handling follow principle of least privilege.
5. Reuse and simplicity: Prefer platform primitives (batching, caching, routing policies) over bespoke implementations.

API STANDARDS

Overview
- All public and internal HTTP APIs must follow the canonical REST/JSON guidelines below. gRPC may be used for high-throughput internal paths with justification.

Versioning
- Use path-based versioning: /v1/, /v2/.
- Breaking changes require a new major version and a migration plan documented in the API CHANGELOG.

Authentication and Authorization
- Hosted API: Bearer tokens (short-lived) + per-token RBAC.
- Internal services: mTLS or short-lived signed JWTs issued by the control plane.

Idempotency and Safety
- POST endpoints that create resources must accept an Idempotency-Key header and persist the key for at least 24 hours.

Error Handling
- Use HTTP status codes consistently. Return a structured error body: {\"code\": string, \"message\": string, \"details\": optional array}.
- Standard error codes: invalid_input, unauthorized, forbidden, rate_limited, overloaded, not_found, internal_error.

Rate Limiting and Quotas
- APIs should return 429 with Retry-After when client rate limits are hit.
- Per-route rate-limiting configs live in the platform config: service->route->limit (rps) and burst.

API Example (summary)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Body: { model: string, input: string, max_tokens: int }
- Responses: 200 (ok), 400 (invalid_input), 429 (rate_limited), 503 (overloaded)

CODING STANDARDS

Languages and Repos
- Primary server languages: Go (control plane, routing), Rust (latency-sensitive runtime components), Python (ML tooling, evals).
- Packaging: Each service repo must have a single clear entrypoint and a Docker image buildable from repo root.

Style and Linting
- Enforce linters and formatters in CI: gofmt+golangci-lint, cargo fmt+clippy, black+ruff for Python.

Testing
- Unit tests required with >70% coverage for core logic.
- Integration tests that exercise API contracts are required on the main branch.
- Performance-critical paths must include microbenchmarks recorded in the benchmarking suite.

Code Review and PRs
- PR checklist: design doc (if >3 files changed or >200 LOC), tests added, CI green, security scan, performance impact noted.

INFRASTRUCTURE STANDARDS (IaC)

Source of truth
- Terraform is the canonical IaC for cloud resources. State stored in S3/GCS with remote locking (DynamoDB/Cloud Storage locks).

Environment parity
- Three primary environments: dev, staging, prod. Config differences must be parameterized (not forked code).

Networking and Security
- Default deny network policies between namespaces. Services requiring cross-namespace access must have documented exceptions and egress whitelists.
- All cloud access uses least-privilege service accounts and short-lived credentials where possible.

Secrets
- Use KMS-backed secret stores (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault). Do not commit secrets to code or repo.

Resource tagging
- Required tags: service, owner, team, cost_center, environment.

IaC Example (snippet)
```
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "redwood-terraform-state"
    key    = "prod/service-x/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
  }
}
```

MODEL-SERVING STANDARDS

Model Artifact Management
- Model artifacts must include: model_id, version, architecture, quantization_profile, training_data_metadata (pointer), and checksum.
- Store artifacts in the model registry (object store with manifest JSON).

Versioning and Rollouts
- Model versions are immutable. Use semantic versioning for model variants (e.g., gpt-small@1.3.0).
- Rollout strategy: canary -> gradual 10/25/50/100% steps with automated quality gates (See Rollout Procedure).

Quantization and Profiles
- Teams must publish quantization profile used for a production model (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed). Profile includes expected degradation metrics and token throughput improvement.

Caching, Batching, and KV Cache
- Runtime must declare supported caching primitives: prefix cache, output cache TTL, and KV cache semantics.
- Default batching behavior: server-side continuous batching with configurable max_batch_size and max_wait_ms.

Rollout Procedure (numbered)
1. Create model manifest and register in the model registry.
2. Deploy model variant to canary pool (<= 5% traffic) with logging and metrics enabled.
3. Run automated evals on production traffic shadow or sampled requests.
4. If quality and performance thresholds pass, increase traffic in steps: 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%.
5. On regression, immediately rollback to previous stable variant and open incident review.

Observability for Models
- Required metrics: request_latency_ms P50/P95/P99, tokens_generated, cache_hit_rate, model_error_rate, memory_utilization (per GPU).
- Traces must include model_id and model_version as attributes.

OBSERVABILITY STANDARDS

Metrics
- Use prometheus client libraries for service metrics. Metric naming: redwood.<service>.<metric> (e.g., redwood.api.generate.requests_total).
- All metrics include labels: service, route, environment, model_id (where applicable), region.

Tracing
- Distributed tracing required for requests crossing service boundaries. Use W3C TraceContext.
- Maximum sampling: prod default 10% for high-volume routes, 100% for error traces.

Logs
- Structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, msg, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, user_token_hash (if present), error_code (if any).
- Log retention: 90 days for prod, 30 days for staging.

Dashboards and Alerts
- Per-service dashboards: request rate, error rate, latency P50/P95/P99, system metrics (CPU, memory, GPU utilization).
- Alerting thresholds are defined in the Alerting Catalog (see related pages). Example SLO alerts:
  - page if 1-minute error rate > 0.5% and traffic > 100r/min
  - page if P99 latency > 2s for more than 5 minutes on the generate route

PERFORMANCE STANDARDS

Latency and Throughput SLOs (guidelines, teams may tighten)
- Hosted API (text generation): P95 latency for text generation <= 1.2s for short requests (<64 tokens) in us-west-2.
- Dedicated GPU pools: target throughput per-GPU must be documented and validated in benchmarking suite.

Benchmarking
- All performance changes that might affect latency or throughput must include benchmark runs recorded in the central benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- Use representative workloads: token length distribution, concurrency patterns.

Capacity Planning
- SRE maintains pool-level capacity targets: 15% headroom for normal operations, 30% for peak planning.

Decision Records (ADRs) \u2014 Summary

| ADR ID | Decision | Date | Owner | Impacted Components |
|--------|----------|------|-------|--------------------|
| ADR-2026-01 | Standardized model artifact manifest + registry | 2026-01-12 | Priya Singh | model-registry, runtime, onboarding |
| ADR-2026-07 | Use path-based API versioning (v1, v2) | 2026-07-05 | Marco Ruiz | public API, SDKs |
| ADR-2026-11 | Adopt continuous batching + KV cache in runtime | 2026-11-02 | Daniel Kim | serving-runtime, scheduler |
| ADR-2026-12 | Default observability sampling (10% prod traces) | 2026-12-10 | Aisha Patel | tracing, dashboards |

Governance and Change Process

- Proposals requiring an ADR: cross-team changes to platform behavior, API breaking changes, or infra changes that affect cost/availability.
- ADR workflow: author creates ADR draft in the adr/ directory in the repo -> 1 week review period -> fixups -> approvers sign-off (service owners + platform leads) -> publish to confluence and link under related_pages.

Operational Runbook Links
- See per-service runbooks for incident response and rollback steps. Key runbooks: runtime-oom-and-restart, api-rate-limits-and-quota-escalation, model-regression-triage.

Appendix: Example Model Manifest (JSON)
```
{
  \"model_id\": \"gpt-redwood-small\",
  \"version\": \"1.3.0\",
  \"architecture\": \"transformer\",
  \"quantization_profile\": \"int8-default\",
  \"artifact_uri\": \"s3://models/redwood/gpt-redwood-small/1.3.0/\",
  \"checksum\": \"sha256:abcd...\",
  \"training_data_metadata\": \"s3://model-metadata/gpt-redwood-small/1.3.0/meta.json\"
}
```
